match.reason: The bank point Layers of the Earth teaches the crust, mantle, core layers and that plates are the crust plus the top of the mantle, at the right depth for Year 8 Victorian Science, though the brief's mention of mantle circulation is covered by a different point, so this is a close match on the layers and plates content.

confirm.reason: The new point joins Earth's four layers (with separate outer and inner core) to mantle convection moving the plates, but no single bank card does both: 'Layers of the Earth' treats the core as one layer and does not explain plate movement, and 'What moves the plates' adds ridge push and slab pull, so it is broader.

draft.title: Earth's layers and moving plates
card: Earth has four layers. From the outside in, they are the crust, the mantle, the outer core and the inner core.
The crust is the thin, rocky outer layer we live on. The mantle is a thick layer of hot rock that is solid but can flow very slowly.
The outer core is liquid metal. The inner core is solid metal and is the hottest, deepest layer.
The crust and upper mantle are broken into large pieces called plates. Hot mantle rock circulates slowly beneath them, and the plates move by a few centimetres a year.
draft.remember: Earth has four layers, and the broken crust and upper mantle form plates that move slowly.

a.q: Which list gives Earth's layers in order from the surface to the centre?
opts: Crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
Crust, outer core, mantle, inner core
Mantle, crust, inner core, outer core
Crust, mantle, inner core, outer core
a.why: Going down from the surface, the order is crust, mantle, outer core, then inner core. The tempting option swaps the two cores, but the liquid outer core surrounds the solid inner core.
a.clue: The solid centre is surrounded by a liquid layer.

b.q: Mia says the plates move because the thin crust floats on the liquid outer core. Which statement best corrects her?
opts: Plates move as hot mantle rock circulates beneath them
Plates move because the solid inner core spins them
Plates move as the liquid outer core pushes up the crust
Plates move because the oceans push on the thin crust
b.why: The plates are the crust and upper mantle, and they move as hot mantle rock circulates slowly beneath them. The outer core is liquid, but it lies below the mantle and is not what the plates sit on.
b.clue: Which layer sits directly under the crust?

wants.brief: A cutaway of Earth showing four labelled layers from the outside in: crust (thin), mantle (thick), outer core (liquid) and inner core (solid).
wants.why: Seeing the layers in order helps students remember their positions and relative thickness.
